name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q01 - Taxonomic family matching of common organisms

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Common Name) List II (Family)
A. Man I. Muscidae
B. Housefly II. Poaceae
C. Mango III. Hominidae
D. Wheat IV. Anacardiaceae

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the taxonomic family of Man.
Man (Homo sapiens) belongs to the genus Homo and the family Hominidae.

Step 2: Determine the taxonomic family of Housefly.
Housefly (Musca domestica) belongs to the genus Musca and the family Muscidae.

Step 3: Determine the taxonomic family of Mango.
Mango (Mangifera indica) belongs to the genus Mangifera and the family Anacardiaceae.

Step 4: Determine the taxonomic family of Wheat.
Wheat (Triticum aestivum) belongs to the genus Triticum and the grass family Poaceae.

Step 5: Synthesize the final matching.
Connecting each organism to its respective family yields: Man with Hominidae, Housefly with Muscidae, Mango with Anacardiaceae, and Wheat with Poaceae.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q02 - Taxonomic order matching of selected organisms

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Organism) List II (Order)
A. Housefly I. Sapindales
B. Mango II. Poales
C. Wheat III. Diptera
D. Man IV. Primata

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the taxonomic order of Housefly.
Housefly (Musca domestica) belongs to the insect order Diptera.

Step 2: Determine the taxonomic order of Mango.
Mango (Mangifera indica) belongs to the dicot order Sapindales.

Step 3: Determine the taxonomic order of Wheat.
Wheat (Triticum aestivum) belongs to the monocot order Poales.

Step 4: Determine the taxonomic order of Man.
Man (Homo sapiens) belongs to the mammalian order Primata.

Step 5: Conclude the overall correspondence.
The correct association pairs Housefly with Diptera, Mango with Sapindales, Wheat with Poales, and Man with Primata.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q03 - Taxonomic categories and representative group matching

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Taxonomic Category) List II (Taxon)
A. Family I. Polymoniales
B. Order II. Angiospermae
C. Class III. Solanaceae
D. Division IV. Dicotyledonae

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the rank for Solanaceae.
Solanaceae is a taxonomic family characterized by vegetative and reproductive features of plant genera such as Solanum, Petunia, and Datura.

Step 2: Evaluate the rank for Polymoniales.
Polymoniales is an order, which represents an assemblage of families like Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae mainly based on floral characters.

Step 3: Evaluate the rank for Dicotyledonae.
Dicotyledonae is a class comprising related orders such as Sapindales and Polymoniales.

Step 4: Evaluate the rank for Angiospermae.
Angiospermae is a division, the category in plants equivalent to phylum in animals, uniting classes sharing broader fundamental characters.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing.
Family matches with Solanaceae, Order matches with Polymoniales, Class matches with Dicotyledonae, and Division matches with Angiospermae.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q04 - Hierarchical taxa and associated biological assemblages

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Group of Genera/Families) List II (Assigned Higher Taxon)
A. Solanum, Petunia, and Datura I. Carnivora
B. Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae II. Felidae
C. Felidae and Canidae III. Polymoniales
D. Panthera and Felis IV. Solanaceae

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the higher taxon for plant genera Solanum, Petunia, and Datura.
The plant genera Solanum, Petunia, and Datura are grouped together into the family Solanaceae based on both vegetative and reproductive characters.

Step 2: Identify the higher taxon for plant families Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae.
The families Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are placed in the order Polymoniales based primarily on floral characteristics.

Step 3: Identify the higher taxon for animal families Felidae and Canidae.
The cat family Felidae and the dog family Canidae are included together in the mammalian order Carnivora.

Step 4: Identify the higher taxon for animal genera Panthera and Felis.
The genus Panthera (lion, leopard, tiger) and the genus Felis (cats) are classified under the family Felidae.

Step 5: Conclude the taxonomic matching.
The correct association matches Solanum, Petunia, and Datura with Solanaceae; Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae with Polymoniales; Felidae and Canidae with Carnivora; and Panthera and Felis with Felidae.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q05 - Historical biologists nomenclature codes and systematics

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Scientist / Term / Code) List II (Contribution / Description)
A. Ernst Mayr I. Provides principles and criteria for scientific naming of plants
B. Carolus Linnaeus II. Pioneered the biological species definition and won the Triple Crown of biology
C. ICBN III. Branch of study that takes into account evolutionary relationships
D. Systematics IV. Proposed binomial nomenclature and authored Systema Naturae

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the contribution of Ernst Mayr.
Ernst Mayr, known as 'The Darwin of the 20th century', pioneered the currently accepted definition of a biological species and received the triple crown of biology (Balzan Prize, International Prize for Biology, and Crafoord Prize).

Step 2: Evaluate the contribution of Carolus Linnaeus.
Carolus Linnaeus introduced the binomial nomenclature system used universally by biologists and titled his famous publication Systema Naturae.

Step 3: Define the role of ICBN.
The International Code for Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN) provides the agreed principles and criteria governing the scientific naming of plants.

Step 4: Define the scope of Systematics.
Systematics is derived from the Latin word 'systema' and deals with the identification, nomenclature, classification, and evolutionary relationships among living organisms.

Step 5: Synthesize the final pairings.
Ernst Mayr matches with pioneering the biological species definition and winning the Triple Crown of biology; Carolus Linnaeus matches with proposing binomial nomenclature and authoring Systema Naturae; ICBN matches with providing agreed principles and criteria for scientific naming of plants; and Systematics matches with the branch of study that takes into account evolutionary relationships.
